t: Old Norse, the North Germanic language of the Viking Age, was spoken from Scandinavia to Iceland, Greenland, the British Isles and Russia, and carved in runes on thousands of memorial stones.
In Iceland, from the 12th to the 14th centuries, it became the language of a great literature, the sagas, the Eddas and skaldic poetry, which preserves the myths and history of the North.
It is the ancestor of Icelandic, Faroese, Norwegian, Danish and Swedish, and through Viking settlement it gave English some of its most everyday words, from sky and egg to they and take.
dyk: English owes some of its most basic words to Old Norse, among them they, them and their, sky, egg, knife, take and window, from vindauga, “wind eye”.
ev: The Viking raid on Lindisfarne opens the Viking Age, which carries Old Norse across the seas
The Rök stone, with the longest known runic inscription, is raised in Sweden
Norse settlers begin to colonise Iceland
The laws of Iceland are first written down in Old Norse
Ari Thorgilsson writes the Book of the Icelanders, the first history in the language
Snorri Sturluson writes the Prose Edda, a handbook of poetry and myth
Njáls saga, the greatest of the Icelandic family sagas, is written
Denmark returns the Codex Regius and Flateyjarbók to Iceland, the first of the medieval manuscripts to go home

f.family: Indo-European: the North Germanic branch of the Germanic languages
f.script: Runes of the Younger Futhark, sixteen letters; from the 11th and 12th centuries the Latin alphabet, with the letters þ and ð
f.earliest: Viking Age runic inscriptions of the 8th and 9th centuries, such as the Rök stone; earlier Proto-Norse inscriptions from about 200 CE
f.status: Extinct; its descendants, Icelandic, Faroese, Norwegian, Danish and Swedish, are spoken by more than 20 million people
